
Two arXiv papers from the RSS feed meet the inclusion threshold. Agentao directly addresses governed runtime architecture and tool-use execution for LLM agents. The behavioral consistency paper provides empirical grounding on cross-task agent reliability relevant to evaluation loop design. Grok social signals were low-quality/unverifiable and are excluded.

## Suggestions

- [Agentao: A Governed Local-First Runtime for Tool-Using LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13574) — Presents a governed, local-first runtime architecture for tool-using LLM agents, addressing execution lifecycle management, tool-use design, and production deployment constraints.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (patterns, orchestration, state management), Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Empirical or practical grounding (case studies, benchmarks, production deployment evidence)

- [Measuring Cross-Task Behavioral Consistency in Language Model Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13598) — Empirical study measuring behavioral consistency of LLM agents across diverse tasks, providing grounding for evaluation loop design and reliability practices in agentic workflows.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Iterative refinement practices (evaluation loops, human-in-the-loop, observability), Empirical or practical grounding (case studies, benchmarks, production deployment evidence), Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (patterns, orchestration, state management)
